$comment: Carlisle control configuration (R5, DECISION_LOG D-027). Real-world claims are unknown unless a source states them; the game area and its boundaries are game-design statements (labelled simplified); membership lists are computed by `npm run data:control-membership -- --dataset carlisle --area carlisle-ws-1`.

provenance.note: OSM maps a railway=signal_box feature with this name. This establishes the mapped building, not its current use or what it controls.

limitations: No imported source states whether the box is in use or whether its work has moved to another centre.
The name says 'Power'; equipment is not inferred from a name (R5). No source describes its panel or workstations.
Not in any imported source; the Sectional Appendix (nr-sectional-appendix) has not been obtained.
OSM maps colour-light signals here (D-022): that describes the signals, not the principles they are worked to.
OSM signal refs share the CE prefix and SMART TD area CL covers the area, but neither establishes control limits (D-008).

membershipProvenance.note: Members are the OSM signals and points on track reached from the playable cuts' inside nodes without crossing a cut (playable-area.json; src/validation/control.ts nodesInPlay). This follows the game-design playable area, not the real box's control limits.

provenance.note: Game design, proposed: one control area for the whole playable area. Whether play is split between several players or AI operators, and where, is undecided. A split will be a game-design choice unless a source establishes a real operational division.

limitations: Carlisle Power Signal Box is mapped inside the playable area (OSM way/1131695849), but no imported source states which signals or points it controls, or whether control has moved elsewhere.

operator.rationale: Human and AI operators use the same control area and the same commands (R6); which one operates it is a session setting.

provenance.note: Game design: either a human or an AI signaller may operate this area.

limitations: No imported source states which signal box or operating centre controls this track.

Game-design boundary at playable-area cut cut-wcml-south-down (extract_boundary): where play stops. Not a real control limit.

limitations: No source identifies the signals at this boundary; OSM signals near the cut have not been assessed for this purpose.
Which cut each timetabled train uses needs the area TIPLOCs mapped to track (28 of 29 unmapped, DATA_GAPS); not derived.
An OSM track ref such as 'Down Main' is a line name, not evidence of the direction trains cross here.
